name: coordination/refusal-unroutable-recipient
description: The refusal that must happen BEFORE the spend (ADR-0016 §6). A staging whose recipient is unnamed, no longer an imported peer, never introduced, suspended, or pinned to something that is not a usable https endpoint cannot be disclosed to anyone — so `dispatch` refuses with the operator's one-shot consent receipt still LIVE. Burning consent on a disclosure that provably cannot leave would be the worst failure available to this surface, and the ordering is what closes it. `409`, not `404`: the staging exists and the consent may exist; what does not exist is a peer to disclose to. `detail` names which of the five cases it was, and is safe to name because the caller staged it.

problem.title: the staged recipient cannot receive a disclosure
problem.detail: this staging named no recipient, so there is nowhere to disclose it
